item.description: - When your anchored AirPods can't switch back to the Mac because another app is holding the Mac's audio output (such as the Android Emulator), the warning now names that app. Quit it or select your AirPods in Control Center > Sound. - The warning is shorter so the menu no longer gets wide. Hover over it to see what to do.

- When your anchored AirPods are connected but their audio is on another device (such as your iPhone) while the Mac is playing sound, the menu bar icon now shows a warning badge and the menu tells you to select them in Control Center > Sound. - AudioAnchor now finds renamed AirPods by the name you gave them, so it can ask them to connect to the Mac again.

- AudioAnchor is now signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so it opens without allowing it in System Settings > Privacy & Security. - Replaced the SimplyCoreAudio and LaunchAtLogin dependencies with direct Core Audio and SMAppService calls.

- Reconnects the anchored Bluetooth device when it is connected to another device, such as AirPods that switched to your iPhone - New app icon - Universal app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs - Fixed: after choosing another output, the previously anchored device was no longer watched - Fixed: choosing an output while disabled did not switch to it - Updated Sparkle and LaunchAtLogin
Requires macOS 13 or later.
If you are using 0.1.x, this version will not be offered as an automatic update. Please download it from this page and replace the app manually.
